brief: 8 mistakes I made as a first-time founder that cost me $250K.

slots.title: 1. Hiring, the mistake
slots.body: I hired five senior engineers before finding product-market fit. The burn rate crushed our runway in eleven months.

slots.title: 2. Building, the trap
slots.body: We spent eight months rebuilding the app for a 'v2.0' launch. Users never asked for half the features.

slots.title: 3. Economics, the blindspot
slots.body: I focused on top-line revenue while our CAC was 3x LTV. We were growing ourselves bankrupt.

slots.title: 4. Deals, the trap
slots.body: One enterprise client demanded bespoke features that broke our roadmap. We became an expensive dev shop.

slots.title: 5. Control, the bottleneck
slots.body: I micromanaged every pixel and email instead of trusting my team. Decisions bottlenecked and velocity died.

slots.title: 6. Equity, the giveaway
slots.body: I gave away 40 percent equity in our pre-seed for $150K. Future rounds diluted me into irrelevance.

slots.headline: Don't Repeat My Errors
slots.subline: Follow for weekly teardowns on building without burning cash.
